The deterministic summary is complete: table_markdown and header_list contain the entire used sheet and are not truncated. Inspect the full structural axes, including later row groups, sparse group anchors, separator rows, and notes/footers, before assigning roles. Keep semantic levels separate. A direct row/column label and a cascading group label are different dimensions even when they share an axis. Each Dimension must represent one concept at one hierarchy level and must have exactly one Relationship with exactly one kind. Never attach two relationship kinds to one Dimension; split the cells into separate dimensions instead. Use only exact canonical R1C1 addresses and ranges. Table 11. Clients who received legal task services(a)(b), Selected characteristics, Legal Aid Commissions, 2023–24
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander status
Cells in this table have been randomly adjusted to avoid the release of confidential data. Discrepancies may occur between sums of the component items and totals.

(a) A client is a person, group, or organisation who received one or more completed services wholly or partially funded under the National Legal Assistance Partnership (NLAP). This is a subset of clients and services received during the reference period. Read more in Methodology, Counting Methodology and Services provided across the sector.

(b) A client is counted once if they received one or more completed services from a single provider during the reference period. Clients who received services from multiple providers (i.e. in different state/territory locations, or across sub-sectors (LACs, ATSILS, CLCs)) will be counted more than once in the combined national data.
(c) Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander status might not be recorded in instances where the service is quick in nature and this information is not required to complete the service.
(d) The age of a client might not be recorded in instances where the service is quick in nature and this information is not required to complete the service.
(e) May include clients with a gender of neither male or female, transgender, intersex or indeterminate, other, unknown or where the gender recorded was not applicable (an organisation, or group).
(f) Problem type represents the primary problem for each service. Read more in Methodology, Data items.
(g) Includes civil law problems not elsewhere classified.
(h) Includes criminal law problems not elsewhere classified.
(i) Includes domestic violence protection orders and domestic/family violence offences. Refer to Table 15 for more information.
(j) Includes consumer, consumer credit and credit and debt. Refer to Table 15 for more information.
(k) Total includes all legal task services. Refer to Table 15 for more information about all problem types.

You are analyzing spreadsheet meaning, not writing an extraction program. Identify observation/value cells, table boundaries, semantic dimensions, header cells, and how each dimension relates to values. Relationship vocabulary: - direct-column: a header directly above values and mapped by column. - direct-row: a header directly left of values and mapped by row. - cascading-column: a hierarchical/super-header above values whose closest preceding label cascades across columns. - cascading-row: a hierarchical/block header whose closest preceding label cascades across rows. The deterministic summary is complete: table_markdown and header_list contain the entire used sheet and are not truncated. Inspect the full structural axes, including later row groups, sparse group anchors, separator rows, and notes/footers, before assigning roles. Keep semantic levels separate. A direct row/column label and a cascading group label are different dimensions even when they share an axis. Each Dimension must represent one concept at one hierarchy level and must have exactly one Relationship with exactly one kind. Never attach two relationship kinds to one Dimension; split the cells into separate dimensions instead. Use only exact canonical R1C1 addresses and ranges.
